title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: k is a base ring (O_k). For a k-module M, V(M) is the k-functor A ↦ Hom_k(M, A), i.e. Spec Sym(M). The previous page proved that morphisms V(N) → V(M) correspond to k-linear maps M → Sym(N) = ⊕_i Sym^i(N). Homogeneous morphisms of degree 1 are exactly those given by M → N, which gives full faithfulness of M ↦ V(M). It then treats morphisms out of a product, ∏_α V(N_α) ≅ V(⊕ N_α), which correspond to u: M → Sym(⊕N_α) = ⊕_{multidegrees (i_α)} ⊗_α Sym^{i_α}(N_α). Write u = Σ u_{(i_α)} accordingly.

This page: for a family of scalars λ = (λ_α) ∈ G_m(A)^I (or the multiplicative monoid A^I), rescaling argument by argument gives u*((λ_α x*_α)) = (u^λ)*(x*_α), where u^λ = Σ (∏_α λ_α^{i_α}) u_{(i_α)}. In other words, u* ∘ ∏ λ_{α,V(N_α)} = (u^λ)*. Hence u* is multihomogeneous of multidegree n = (n_α) iff u factors through ⊗_α Sym^{n_α}(N_α).

In particular, homogeneity of degree 1 in each argument amounts to u: M → ⊗_α N_α. Such a u* is then automatically multilinear, since it is linear in each variable with the others fixed. So multilinear pairings ∏ V(N_α) → V(M) correspond to linear maps M → ⊗_α N_α, and bilinear pairings V(N) × V(N') → V(M) correspond to M → N ⊗ N'.

Purpose: the next page takes M = N = N'. A bilinear composition law on V(M) is then the same as a comultiplication Δ: M → M ⊗ M, with associativity, commutativity and unit matching the coalgebra axioms. This is the functorial dictionary 'algebra structures on the vector-group functor V(M) = coalgebra structures on M'. It presumably prepares divided-power and Hopf-algebra constructions for the PD de Rham complex.
errors: On the previous page, 'Sym^i(⊕N_α) = ⊗_α Sym^i(N_α)' is a slip. The correct statement is Sym(⊕N_α) = ⊕_{(i_α)} ⊗_α Sym^{i_α}(N_α) (a restricted tensor product if I is infinite). The current page uses the correct multidegree decomposition, so nothing downstream is affected.
Minor gap: to detect homogeneity by scalars λ one must allow λ in arbitrary A (e.g. A = k[t, t^{-1}]), not just λ ∈ k. This is implicit in the functorial setting, so it is fine.

ideas.what: Morphisms of products of vector-bundle functors ∏V(N_α) → V(M) correspond to M → Sym(⊕N_α); multihomogeneous components correspond to the multidegree decomposition via the action of scalars.
ideas.modern_name: Grading/G_m^I-action on the linear scheme V(M); polynomial laws (Roby)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Roby's polynomial laws 1963; Demazure–Gabriel; SGA 3 Exp. I)
ideas.where_published: EGA II §1.7 (V(E)), SGA 3 Exp. I (W(E), V(E) and gradings)

ideas.what: Multilinear maps ∏V(N_α) → V(M) correspond to linear maps M → ⊗N_α; bilinear maps V(N) × V(N') → V(M) correspond to M → N ⊗ N'.
ideas.modern_name: Duality between tensor products and multilinear morphisms of vector group schemes
ideas.where_published: Analogous statements in SGA 3 Exp. I

ideas.what: Preparing the correspondence: bilinear laws on V(M) correspond to coalgebra structures on M.
ideas.modern_name: Cartier duality style dictionary: algebra-object structures on V(M) are coalgebras

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but entirely standard functorial linear algebra (multihomogeneous morphisms of V(M), multilinear maps vs. tensor products), serving as groundwork for coalgebra/divided-power constructions. Nothing new.
transcription_corrections: First line likely reads 'on voit que si λ = (λ_α) ∈ G_m(A)^I' (or the multiplicative monoid of A); 'A^*_∞' is a misreading.
The parenthetical reads roughly '(prenant aussi comme définition « linéaire en chaque variable (en fixant les autres) »)', not 'prenant aussi de dérivation fonctionnelle en une variable'.
'accouplements bil.' probably means multilinear for the ∏V(N_α) case ('accouplements multil.').
